consolidation_review_notes.SU-CP-02_general_principles: Drug Nomenclature + Phases of Clinical Drug Testing combined. REVIEWED, not ambiguous: both are thin, orientation-level definitional content (naming conventions; trial-phase vocabulary) rather than independently testable clinical competencies, matching the treatment given to comparably thin foundational content in Chapters A/C (e.g., SU-A-02 Overview of Anesthesia).
consolidation_review_notes.SU-CP-09_pharmacodynamics_ti: Pharmacodynamics (dose-response/efficacy/potency) + Effectiveness and Safety + Therapeutic Indices combined, even though the printed 'Effects of Drugs on Receptors' topic (CP.S02.T07) sits physically between the two halves in the source and is represented as its own separate unit (SU-CP-10). REVIEWED, not ambiguous: the Pharmacodynamics/Effectiveness/TI topics form one continuous conceptual thread (all describe magnitude/safety of the same dose-response curve, sharing Figures 1 and 4-6), while Effects of Drugs on Receptors tests a mechanistically distinct skill (agonist/antagonist classification from a binding mechanism, not curve-magnitude interpretation).
consolidation_review_notes.SU-CP-13_14_15_adr_split: The CP.S04 same-page merge (Adverse Drug Reactions + Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology) was split into three units rather than two, pulling 'Drug Interactions' out into its own unit (SU-CP-14) despite it being a topic child of the 'Adverse Drug Reactions' portion. REVIEWED, not ambiguous: Drug Interactions carries an extensive, distinct sidebar of named clinically-significant interaction pairs that is a high-yield testable surface in its own right, warranting separate coverage-weight/question-planning treatment from the ADR-classification-and-reporting workflow tested in SU-CP-13.
consolidation_review_notes.SU-CP-15_16_ans_opioid_split: The Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology portion of the CP.S04 merge nests 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain' under it in the printed TOC layout (as a third sub-bullet alongside Parasympathetic/Sympathetic NS), but the two are thematically unrelated (ANS receptor physiology vs. an opioid-prescribing clinical guideline). REVIEWED, not ambiguous: kept as separate units (SU-CP-15, SU-CP-16) per the same-page-merge protocol's guidance to resolve based on confirmed body content and thematic coherence rather than raw TOC indentation.
